nameHistory.name: C u M C back KIDZ!!!

teams.commentary: Miami took over the No. 1 spot in college football after Saturday's chaos, and the Cartel takes over first here the same way: by winning while the teams around it tripped. Mike D. made the first trade of the season on Thursday, sending Cam Skattebo, Alvin Kamara, Juwan Johnson and Denzel Boston to Frum for Bhayshul Tuten, Colston Loveland and the Steelers defense, and the return was immediate. Tuten scored 22.7 in the flex, the Steelers put up 11, and Loveland scored 15.5 on the bench, so the new arrivals combined for 49 points while the four players he sent away scored about 16, only 2 of them in Frum's lineup. Isaiah Likely added 20.9, Jayden Daniels 21, and the win over Hess was the most comfortable of the week. The worries are Derrick Henry at 4.5 and a receiver room that got thin in a hurry: Terry McLaurin is out, Ja'Marr Chase was on a bye, and the next man up is Darius Cooper, with Tyreek Hill, whom Mike D. scooped up after Frum cut him, sitting on the bench with a questionable tag.

teams.name: DINO NUGGETS

nameHistory.name: The Man the Myth the Legend

teams.commentary: Baker lost first place by six-tenths of a point, and the committee would like to direct everyone's attention to the tight end slot, where the same crime keeps happening. Harold Fannin Jr., the $18 keeper, scored 1.4 in the lineup while Hunter Henry scored 12.8 on the bench, the second straight week Henry has outscored him by double digits from the pine. Keon Coleman also scored 13.9 on the bench while Dallas Goedert started in the flex, so there were two different ways to win this game and Baker found neither. In fairness, Jahmyr Gibbs, Justin Jefferson and Jameson Williams were all on bye, and Trevor Lawrence's 27.3 kept the Dino Nuggets close. Baker also cut Kyler Murray a week after Murray scored 18 on his bench, a bold move for a team whose backup running back, MarShawn Lloyd, scored 1 and projects for nothing.

teams.name: Ammonia Coladas
teams.commentary: The Coladas won with the tenth-best score of the week, which is the sort of thing that happens when you play the twelfth. Drake Maye scored 23.8 and Malik Nabers 22.5, and that was more or less the whole show: Bucky Irving managed 5.9, Brian Robinson Jr. scored 2, and Tyler Higbee, picked up to cover a Sam LaPorta bye, scored 2.2. The pickup that worked, Roschon Johnson, scored 13.5 on the bench behind Robinson, but Mark won by 4.4 so the committee will let it slide, this once. A win is a win, and Mark is 4-2 and third, but the backfield behind Irving now projects around 3 a game with Kyle Monangai out and Josh Jacobs still on IR. Mark gets Baker next, then the second-hardest remaining schedule in the league.

teams.name: $200 Dolla Holla
teams.commentary: There it is. Hearn has owned the best all-play record in the league all season and had nothing to show for it, and this week he finally put up the top score, 112.6, beat all eleven teams in the all-play, and climbed two spots to fourth. James Cook went for 22.8, D'Andre Swift for 21, and George Kittle added 15.4 in the 49ers' Monday night win. Caleb Williams came back from his injury and threw for 305 yards on Hearn's bench, but Brock Purdy outscored him by less than a point, so for once the quarterback call was right. The Colts defense, a fresh pickup, scored 5 on a day Indianapolis lost to the previously winless Titans and fired its general manager. Hearn is 3-3 with a luck number that says he should be at least 4-2; with Deebo Samuel out and Alec Pierce on IR, the receivers behind A.J. Brown and Christian Watson project around 6 a game, which is serviceable if not exciting.

teams.name: Captain Casper's Low Risk Tacos

nameHistory.name: Coach Matty Ps D In Swishs V

teams.commentary: The Tacos survived Frum by 2.2, and the committee has some questions about how. C.J. Stroud, whom Brett picked up after Mike D. let him go, threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns in London and scored 22.9 on Brett's bench while Josh Allen started and scored 18.3. Taylor Swift has the number one song in the world, and her husband scored 7.3 while Kyle Pitts scored 20.5 on Brett's bench,. RJ Harvey added 13.1 on the bench, too, so Brett left more than 22 points sitting in a game he won by barely two. DeVonta Smith came back with 17 and Keenan Allen added 12.2, which helped, and Dameon Pierce scored 13 filling in for Aaron Jones on bye. Saquon Barkley is still out, and the receiver behind DeVonta and Chris Olave, Keenan Allen, projects under 3 a game despite this week's 12, so the wide receiver trade Brett keeps talking about is starting to look less like a luxury.

teams.name: Papas McButt Nuggets

nameHistory.name: Why dont you just call them?

teams.commentary: Jordan once named his team thank you for the blessings, and the blessings have officially run out. The luckiest team in the league posted the lowest score of the week, lost to all eleven teams in the all-play, and lost to Mark by 4.4 with Carnell Tate's 16 and Stefon Diggs' 13.4 on the bench behind Tyler Allgeier's 5.3 in the flex, either of which wins the game. The Dodgers' three-peat bid ended in a four-game sweep this week; Jordan's run at first place ended in an 0-11. The Jaguars defense went negative while C.J. Stroud carved it up in London, and Jordan cut the Browns defense a week after it scored 11 on his bench. Jordan has left 134 points on his bench this season, about 20 more than anyone else. With Jeremiyah Love out and Tyler Warren out, the backup running back projects around 3 a game, and the six-way logjam at 4-2 says Jordan is one more week like this from the middle of the pack.

teams.name: Christopher Dootron
teams.commentary: Sam is 4-2 with a losing all-play record, which is either a strategy or a horoscope, and this week he won by 1.2 over Danny with the eighth-best score. Bijan Robinson was the bust of the week at 6.3, but Tyler Shough threw for 26.8 and Tyler Bass, the kicker Sam picked up, scored 17. Bass replaced Will Reichard, who scored 16 for him last week, because Sam has now made 24 pickups this season and apparently treats the kicker slot like a rental car. He also cut Kirk Cousins, who promptly scored 18.4 for Foy. The real problem remains running back: with Jordan Mason on IR there is literally nobody behind Bijan and Omarion Hampton, and Sam is one tweaked hamstring away from starting a receiver at running back.

teams.commentary: Foy scored the fourth-best total of the week and lost anyway, which is how it goes when you draw the top score. The Chiefs defense, his pickup from a few weeks back, finally got a start and led the league with 14 in a 22-6 win over the winless Chargers, and Kirk Cousins, picked up after Sam cut him, scored 18.4 filling in for Jared Goff on bye. Daniel Carlson even kicked 14, which in the Table Shepherd kicker saga counts as a happy ending. The problem was Kyren Williams at 8.2 on a projection over 19. With David Montgomery out and Jacory Croskey-Merritt on IR, there is nobody behind Kyren and Blake Corum, and Foy has a surplus of receivers once Amon-Ra is back: a back-for-receiver deal is the most obvious move in the league.

teams.name: Quintosss... Amigo?
teams.commentary: Auburn beat No. 1 Georgia on a walk-off field goal on Saturday, and Jeff did the fantasy version on Sunday, beating the first-place team by six-tenths of a point. He did it with a perfect lineup, zero points left on the bench, and nine starters who all scored between 7 and 13, which is either balance or a lack of upside depending on your mood. Harrison Butker kicked 13 in his return from the bye, the Ravens defense added 10, and Khalil Shakir scored 11.4 in the flex. The infirmary is getting crowded: Jalen Hurts is on IR, Breece Hall, Quinshon Judkins and Rashee Rice are out, and the healthy backs after Tony Pollard project under 2 a game. Jeff has the softest remaining schedule in the league and a win over the first-place team. Nobody tell him the question mark is still in the team name.

teams.name: Los Desperados Sudados
teams.commentary: Danny once called his team Back to the Well, and he keeps going back to the same well: losing close games with points on the bench. This week he lost by 1.2 to Sam with DJ Moore, who was out, sitting in the flex for a zero, while Rachaad White scored 13.7 on the bench. Dalton Kincaid and Rome Odunze would have won it too. Aaron Rodgers, picked up for the Burrow bye, gave him 15.9, and Matthew Golden went for 19.4, but Danny is now 1-5 with a winning all-play record and the worst luck number in the league by a distance. At some point the curse is just a lineup problem wearing a costume. The running back depth behind Ashton Jeanty and Chase Brown is White at under 6 a game, with Travis Etienne and Isiah Pacheco both on IR.

teams.name: For Heaven Sakes, Woman
teams.commentary: Hess picked up Blake Grupe to kick for him this week, and Grupe made a 44-yard field goal and then got hurt on the ensuing kickoff, which is a perfect summary of how the Heavenly Woman's luck has gone. Grupe finished with 4 and is now on IR. The bigger damage was at receiver, where Davante Adams scored 5.4 while Tre Tucker scored 24.2 on the bench, the biggest bench bomb of the week in a game Hess lost by 21. Christian McCaffrey scored two touchdowns on Monday night for 26.2, and Keaton Mitchell, the back Hess picked up from Mark's scrap heap, started and scored 0.4. Hess also cut Cameron Dicker, his kicker all season, to make room for the kicker who lasted one kickoff. With Davante Adams out and Jayden Reed on IR, the next receiver projects under 5 a game, and the running back behind McCaffrey and TreVeyon Henderson isn't much better.

teams.commentary: Street Fighter topped the box office this weekend, and Frum walked into the league's first trade like a guy who picked the wrong character. He sent Bhayshul Tuten, Colston Loveland and the Steelers defense to Mike D., and they scored 22.7, 15.5 and 11 for the Cartel. In return he got Alvin Kamara, Cam Skattebo, Juwan Johnson and Denzel Boston, started Johnson and Boston for a combined 2, and left Kamara's 13.9 on the bench in a game he lost by 2.2. Starting Kamara over Woody Marks would have won it; so would Jaylen Waddle over Boston. The silver linings were real: Germie Bernard, picked up this week, scored 20.2 in the flex, and Kenneth Walker went for 26.9. Frum now has more running backs than he can start, Kamara, Skattebo, Kendre Miller and Ollie Gordon II among them, and a receiver room that needs every one of them to become a wide receiver by Friday.

commentary.intro: Olivia Rodrigo and Chappell Roan both put out new music on Friday, and Fadunkadunk had a collaboration of its own: Mike D. and Frum made the first trade of the season, four Cartel players for three Bellies, and by Monday night it was clear only one of them had a hit. Mike D. takes over first place. College football saw a record five of the top seven teams lose on Saturday, and the fantasy weekend was nearly as rude to the favorites: Jordan posted the lowest score in the league and fell from third to sixth, and Baker lost his grip on first by six-tenths of a point. With the Lions, Bengals and Vikings on bye, nobody cleared 113, the lowest winning high score of the season, and four games were decided by less than five points. Six teams are now 4-2, Hearn finally got the top score his all-play record has been promising, and Danny lost a one-point game with an injured receiver in his flex.

awards.closest: Jeff over Baker by 0.6, with Hunter Henry's 12.8 on Baker's bench behind Harold Fannin Jr.'s 1.4. Auburn beat No. 1 Georgia with a walk-off field goal on Saturday; Jeff beat the No. 1 team with a lineup card on Sunday.
awards.questionableStart: Danny started DJ Moore, who was out, in his flex and lost by 1.2 while Rachaad White scored 13.7 on the bench. That isn't bad luck, that's a forfeit.
awards.worstDefense: Jordan's Jaguars went negative on the same day C.J. Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns against them in London.
awards.highScore: Hearn, 112.6, his first top score of the season and a perfect 11-0 all-play week.
awards.lowScore: Jordan, 82.3, and nearly 20 points on the bench.
awards.luckiestWin: Mark won with the tenth-best score of the week because he drew the twelfth.
awards.toughestLoss: Foy scored 104.1, fourth-best in the league, and ran into the week's top score.
awards.blowout: Mike D. over Hess by 21.2, the biggest margin of a week where nobody could get separation.
awards.bestDefense: Foy's Chiefs led all defenses with 14 in a 22-6 win over the winless Chargers.
awards.boom: Germie Bernard, picked up this week, scored 20.2 for Frum on a projection of 7.8.
awards.bust: Bijan Robinson, projected 21.3, scored 6.3 for Sam, who won anyway.
awards.benchBomb: Hess benched Tre Tucker (24.2) for Davante Adams (5.4), an 18.8-point swing in a game he lost by 21.

commentary.outro:
Week 7 brings a pair of top-five showdowns: Baker against Mark, second against third, and Brett A. against Jordan, the reigning champ against the league's most generous bench. Mike D. defends first place against Danny, who will need to start healthy players to have a chance. Hearn gets Sam, the best all-play record in the league against a 4-2 team with a losing one, Foy gets Hess, and Jeff takes his upset win to Frum.

Trade Desk: the first deal of the season is in, and the early grades are not close. Mike D. turned four spare parts into three starters, and Frum got a running back glut and a Week 6 loss by two points. To be fair to Frum, the deal makes sense if he uses it, because he now has backs to sell and the league is full of buyers. Sam has nobody behind Bijan and Hampton and has receivers to spare; Kamara for Luther Burden III fixes both teams. Foy has nobody behind Kyren and Corum and a receiver surplus; Cam Skattebo for Courtland Sutton is a clean swap. Jeff and Mark need backs too, and Jordan's depth chart behind Jonathan Taylor is a rumor. Move of the week: Mike D.'s trade, 49 points from the incoming players in Week 6 alone. Anti-move of the week: Frum starting the two new players who scored a combined 2 and benching the one who scored 13.9, then losing by 2.2.

Luck Index: Danny is 1-5 with a 34-32 all-play record and the worst luck number in the league by a wide margin, though he did his best this week to earn it. Jordan and Sam are the luckiest, both 4-2 with losing all-play records, and Hearn is still 3-3 with the best all-play in the league. The regression is coming. Rankings and commentary refresh every Tuesday morning once ESPN finalizes the week.
